**Q1: Old horizontal row.**  
The horizontal arrangement lets the eye sweep left-to-right across all three complexes at constant vertical position, making curve-crossing and parallel-rise patterns immediate. The inverted-triangle layout forces vertical saccades that break the comparison flow, and the 50% height increase buys nothing—each panel's internal y-range is fixed by its data, so white space above/below short ladders is wasted. JCTC readers scan figures for trends across systems; prioritize that over symmetry.

**Q2: Short tick + number on the right spine (option iv).**  
Panel-title numbers (ii) bloat titles and force the reader to decode which number belongs to which curve; caption-only (iii) requires flipping between figure and text during analysis. The right-spine tick is unambiguous (it terminates the dotted line at a quantified y-value), survives shrinking because it's structurally part of the axis, and doesn't collide with data or need a white knockout box.

**Q3: Option (iii)—direct annotation in panel (a), no footer.**  
Write "6-31G*" next to the solid curve and "aug-cc-pVDZ" next to the dashed curve inside panel (a) at a vertical position with no data collision (e.g., between MP2 and CCSD if space permits). Once the reader sees solid=6-31G* in (a), pattern recognition applies it to (b) and (c) without re-reading. Footer keys for line styles work in time-series plots where x varies; here every panel has identical x (the method ladder), so redundant global keys feel like instructions rather than data.

**Unnoticed defect:**  
The orange dotted line in Figure 5(d)'s bar chart uses the same visual code (dotted orange) as the ω-B97X-V reference in panels (a)-(c), but in (d) it presumably marks something else (a ratio axis gridline? a threshold?). If it's unrelated, use a different color or style; if it *is* the DFT reference carried into the bar chart, the bars should acknowledge it structurally (e.g., bars measured *from* that line, not from zero).

**VERDICT: REVISE**
